# Project 1: RNA-seq Differential Expression Analysis Pipeline

## Problem Statement

A research team has RNA-seq data from cancer patients (treatment vs control) and needs to:
1. Identify differentially expressed genes
2. Perform functional enrichment analysis
3. Generate publication-quality figures
4. Create an interactive report for collaborators

## Complete Workflow

```{r}
# Project structure
# rnaseq_project/
#   ├── data/
#   │   ├── counts.csv
#   │   └── metadata.csv
#   ├── scripts/
#   │   ├── 01_qc.R
#   │   ├── 02_deseq2.R
#   │   └── 03_enrichment.R
#   ├── results/
#   └── report.Rmd

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(DESeq2)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(pheatmap)
library(EnhancedVolcano)
library(ggplot2)
library(DT)

# ==================== Step 1: Load and Prepare Data ====================

# Read count matrix
counts <- read.csv("data/counts.csv", row.names = 1)
head(counts)

# Read metadata
metadata <- read.csv("data/metadata.csv", row.names = 1)
metadata$condition <- factor(metadata$condition, levels = c("control", "treatment"))
metadata$batch <- factor(metadata$batch)

# Ensure sample order matches
counts <- counts[, rownames(metadata)]
all(colnames(counts) == rownames(metadata))

# ==================== Step 2: Quality Control ====================

# Calculate library sizes
lib_sizes <- colSums(counts)
metadata$lib_size <- lib_sizes

# Plot library sizes
ggplot(metadata, aes(x = sample_id, y = lib_size/1e6, fill = condition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Library Sizes",
       x = "Sample",
       y = "Total Reads (Millions)") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1")

# Filter low count genes
# Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples
keep <- rowSums(counts >= 10) >= 3
counts_filtered <- counts[keep, ]
cat("Genes before filtering:", nrow(counts), "\n")
cat("Genes after filtering:", nrow(counts_filtered), "\n")

# ==================== Step 3: DESeq2 Analysis ====================

# Create DESeq2 object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts_filtered,
  colData = metadata,
  design = ~ batch + condition  # Adjust for batch effect
)

# Run DESeq2
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Get results
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "treatment", "control"))
res_ordered <- res[order(res$padj), ]

# Summary
summary(res)

# Convert to data frame for downstream analysis
res_df <- as.data.frame(res_ordered) %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj))

# Add gene symbols
library(AnnotationDbi)
res_df$symbol <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
                        keys = res_df$gene_id,
                        column = "SYMBOL",
                        keytype = "ENSEMBL",
                        multiVals = "first")

# Save results
write.csv(res_df, "results/deseq2_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Define significant genes
sig_genes <- res_df %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1)

cat("Significant genes:", nrow(sig_genes), "\n")
cat("Up-regulated:", sum(sig_genes$log2FoldChange > 0), "\n")
cat("Down-regulated:", sum(sig_genes$log2FoldChange < 0), "\n")

# ==================== Step 4: Visualization ====================

# 1. Volcano Plot
volcano <- EnhancedVolcano(
  res_df,
  lab = res_df$symbol,
  x = 'log2FoldChange',
  y = 'padj',
  title = 'Treatment vs Control',
  pCutoff = 0.05,
  FCcutoff = 1,
  pointSize = 2.0,
  labSize = 4.0,
  col = c('grey30', 'forestgreen', 'royalblue', 'red2'),
  colAlpha = 0.7,
  legendPosition = 'right',
  drawConnectors = TRUE,
  widthConnectors = 0.5,
  max.overlaps = 20
)

ggsave("results/volcano_plot.png", volcano, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

# 2. MA Plot
ggplot(res_df, aes(x = log2(baseMean), y = log2FoldChange)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = padj < 0.05), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("grey", "red")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "MA Plot",
       x = "Mean Expression (log2)",
       y = "Log2 Fold Change",
       color = "Significant")

ggsave("results/ma_plot.png", width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# 3. PCA Plot
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)

pca_data <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("condition", "batch"), returnData = TRUE)
percentVar <- round(100 * attr(pca_data, "percentVar"))

ggplot(pca_data, aes(PC1, PC2, color = condition, shape = batch)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", percentVar[2], "% variance")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1")

ggsave("results/pca_plot.png", width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# 4. Heatmap of top genes
top_genes <- head(res_ordered, 50)
mat <- assay(vsd)[rownames(top_genes), ]

# Annotate with gene symbols
rownames(mat) <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
                       keys = rownames(mat),
                       column = "SYMBOL",
                       keytype = "ENSEMBL",
                       multiVals = "first")

# Scale by row
mat_scaled <- t(scale(t(mat)))

# Create annotation
annotation_col <- data.frame(
  Condition = metadata$condition,
  Batch = metadata$batch,
  row.names = rownames(metadata)
)

# Plot heatmap
png("results/heatmap_top50.png", width = 800, height = 1000)
pheatmap(
  mat_scaled,
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  show_rownames = TRUE,
  show_colnames = TRUE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50),
  main = "Top 50 Differentially Expressed Genes"
)
dev.off()

# ==================== Step 5: Functional Enrichment ====================

# Get up and down regulated genes separately
up_genes <- sig_genes %>%
  filter(log2FoldChange > 1) %>%
  pull(gene_id)

down_genes <- sig_genes %>%
  filter(log2FoldChange < -1) %>%
  pull(gene_id)

# Convert ENSEMBL to ENTREZ for enrichment
up_entrez <- bitr(up_genes, fromType = "ENSEMBL", toType = "ENTREZID",
                  OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db)$ENTREZID

down_entrez <- bitr(down_genes, fromType = "ENSEMBL", toType = "ENTREZID",
                    OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db)$ENTREZID

# GO Enrichment - Biological Process
ego_up <- enrichGO(
  gene = up_entrez,
  OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db,
  ont = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff = 0.05
)

ego_down <- enrichGO(
  gene = down_entrez,
  OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db,
  ont = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff = 0.05
)

# KEGG Pathway Enrichment
kegg_up <- enrichKEGG(
  gene = up_entrez,
  organism = 'hsa',
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05
)

kegg_down <- enrichKEGG(
  gene = down_entrez,
  organism = 'hsa',
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05
)

# Visualize enrichment
png("results/go_enrichment_up.png", width = 1000, height = 800)
dotplot(ego_up, showCategory = 20) +
  ggtitle("GO Enrichment - Up-regulated Genes")
dev.off()

png("results/go_enrichment_down.png", width = 1000, height = 800)
dotplot(ego_down, showCategory = 20) +
  ggtitle("GO Enrichment - Down-regulated Genes")
dev.off()

# Save enrichment results
write.csv(as.data.frame(ego_up), "results/go_enrichment_up.csv")
write.csv(as.data.frame(kegg_up), "results/kegg_enrichment_up.csv")

# ==================== Step 6: Interactive Report ====================

# Create interactive data table
datatable(
  res_df,
  filter = 'top',
  extensions = 'Buttons',
  options = list(
    dom = 'Bfrtip',
    buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel'),
    pageLength = 25
  ),
  caption = "DESeq2 Results - All Genes"
) %>%
  formatRound(columns = c('baseMean', 'log2FoldChange', 'lfcSE', 'stat'), digits = 3) %>%
  formatSignif(columns = c('pvalue', 'padj'), digits = 3) %>%
  formatStyle(
    'padj',
    backgroundColor = styleInterval(0.05, c('lightcoral', 'white'))
  ) %>%
  formatStyle(
    'log2FoldChange',
    backgroundColor = styleInterval(c(-1, 1), c('lightblue', 'white', 'lightcoral'))
  )

# ==================== Step 7: Generate Report ====================

# Save session info
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "results/session_info.txt")

# Create summary statistics
summary_stats <- list(
  total_genes_tested = nrow(res_df),
  significant_genes = nrow(sig_genes),
  up_regulated = sum(sig_genes$log2FoldChange > 1),
  down_regulated = sum(sig_genes$log2FoldChange < -1),
  mean_lib_size = mean(metadata$lib_size),
  date_analyzed = Sys.Date()
)

saveRDS(summary_stats, "results/summary_stats.rds")
```

library(DT)
library(kableExtra)

# Load results
res_df <- read.csv("results/deseq2_results.csv")
summary_stats <- readRDS("results/summary_stats.rds")
```

# Executive Summary

This report presents the results of differential gene expression analysis comparing treatment vs control conditions.

- **Total genes tested**: `r format(summary_stats$total_genes_tested, big.mark=",")`
- **Significant genes**: `r summary_stats$significant_genes`
- **Up-regulated**: `r summary_stats$up_regulated`
- **Down-regulated**: `r summary_stats$down_regulated`

# Project 2: Customer Churn Prediction System

## Problem Statement

A telecom company wants to predict customer churn to implement retention strategies. Build a complete ML pipeline including:
1. Data cleaning and feature engineering
2. Model training and evaluation
3. Feature importance analysis
4. Deployment-ready prediction API

## Complete Workflow

```{r}
# ==================== Step 1: Setup and Data Loading ====================

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(vip)
library(themis)
library(plotly)
library(DALEX)

# Simulate customer data (in practice, load from database)
set.seed(123)
n <- 5000

customers <- tibble(
  customer_id = paste0("CUST", 1:n),
  tenure_months = sample(1:72, n, replace = TRUE),
  monthly_charges = rnorm(n, 70, 20),
  total_charges = tenure_months * monthly_charges + rnorm(n, 0, 100),
  contract_type = sample(c("Month-to-month", "One year", "Two year"),
                        n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2)),
  payment_method = sample(c("Credit card", "Bank transfer", "Electronic check"),
                         n, replace = TRUE),
  internet_service = sample(c("DSL", "Fiber", "No"), n, replace = TRUE),
  online_security = sample(c("Yes", "No"), n, replace = TRUE),
  tech_support = sample(c("Yes", "No"), n, replace = TRUE),
  streaming_tv = sample(c("Yes", "No"), n, replace = TRUE),
  num_support_calls = rpois(n, lambda = 2),
  avg_call_duration = rgamma(n, shape = 2, scale = 10)
)

# Generate churn based on features (realistic patterns)
customers <- customers %>%
  mutate(
    churn_prob = plogis(
      -2 +
      -0.05 * tenure_months +
      0.02 * monthly_charges +
      -1.5 * (contract_type == "Two year") +
      -0.8 * (contract_type == "One year") +
      0.8 * (payment_method == "Electronic check") +
      0.3 * num_support_calls +
      -0.5 * (online_security == "Yes")
    ),
    churned = rbinom(n, 1, churn_prob),
    churned = factor(churned, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
  ) %>%
  select(-churn_prob)

# ==================== Step 2: Exploratory Data Analysis ====================

# Churn rate
churn_rate <- mean(customers$churned == "Yes")
cat("Overall churn rate:", round(churn_rate * 100, 2), "%\n")

# Churn by contract type
churn_by_contract <- customers %>%
  group_by(contract_type, churned) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)

ggplot(churn_by_contract, aes(x = contract_type, y = pct, fill = churned)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Churn Rate by Contract Type",
       x = "Contract Type",
       y = "Percentage",
       fill = "Churned") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1")

# Tenure distribution by churn
ggplot(customers, aes(x = tenure_months, fill = churned)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, position = "dodge", alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Tenure Distribution by Churn Status",
       x = "Tenure (months)",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Churned")

# Correlation plot
library(corrplot)
numeric_vars <- customers %>%
  select(tenure_months, monthly_charges, total_charges,
         num_support_calls, avg_call_duration)

corrplot(cor(numeric_vars), method = "color", type = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black", number.cex = 0.7)

# ==================== Step 3: Feature Engineering ====================

customers_fe <- customers %>%
  mutate(
    # Create features
    charge_per_month = total_charges / (tenure_months + 1),
    tenure_group = case_when(
      tenure_months <= 12 ~ "0-1 year",
      tenure_months <= 36 ~ "1-3 years",
      tenure_months <= 60 ~ "3-5 years",
      TRUE ~ "5+ years"
    ),
    has_online_services = (online_security == "Yes" |
                          tech_support == "Yes" |
                          streaming_tv == "Yes"),
    support_intensity = num_support_calls * avg_call_duration,
    high_value_customer = monthly_charges > median(monthly_charges)
  )

# ==================== Step 4: Model Training with tidymodels ====================

# Split data
set.seed(123)
split <- initial_split(customers_fe, prop = 0.75, strata = churned)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data <- testing(split)

# Create cross-validation folds
folds <- vfold_cv(train_data, v = 5, strata = churned)

# Define recipe
churn_recipe <- recipe(churned ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  # Remove ID
  step_rm(customer_id) %>%
  # Handle missing values
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  # Create dummy variables
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  # Normalize
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  # Handle class imbalance with SMOTE
  step_smote(churned)

# Check recipe
prep(churn_recipe) %>% bake(new_data = NULL)

# Define models

# 1. Logistic Regression
logistic_spec <- logistic_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

# 2. Random Forest
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 1000) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

# 3. XGBoost
xgb_spec <- boost_tree(
  trees = 1000,
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune(),
  sample_size = tune(),
  mtry = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune()
) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

# Create workflows
logistic_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(churn_recipe) %>%
  add_model(logistic_spec)

rf_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(churn_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)

xgb_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(churn_recipe) %>%
  add_model(xgb_spec)

# ==================== Step 5: Hyperparameter Tuning ====================

# Set up parallel processing
library(doParallel)
cl <- makeCluster(detectCores() - 1)
registerDoParallel(cl)

# Tune logistic regression
logistic_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  penalty(),
  mixture(),
  size = 20
)

logistic_tune <- tune_grid(
  logistic_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = logistic_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy, precision, recall),
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

# Tune random forest
rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  mtry(range = c(3, 10)),
  min_n(),
  size = 20
)

rf_tune <- tune_grid(
  rf_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = rf_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy, precision, recall),
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

# Tune XGBoost
xgb_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  loss_reduction(),
  sample_size = sample_prop(),
  finalize(mtry(), train_data),
  learn_rate(),
  size = 30
)

xgb_tune <- tune_grid(
  xgb_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = xgb_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy, precision, recall),
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

stopCluster(cl)

# ==================== Step 6: Model Evaluation ====================

# Compare models
logistic_best <- select_best(logistic_tune, "roc_auc")
rf_best <- select_best(rf_tune, "roc_auc")
xgb_best <- select_best(xgb_tune, "roc_auc")

# Show best metrics
show_best(logistic_tune, "roc_auc", n = 1)
show_best(rf_tune, "roc_auc", n = 1)
show_best(xgb_tune, "roc_auc", n = 1)

# Finalize workflows with best parameters
final_logistic <- finalize_workflow(logistic_wf, logistic_best)
final_rf <- finalize_workflow(rf_wf, rf_best)
final_xgb <- finalize_workflow(xgb_wf, xgb_best)

# Fit on training data
logistic_fit <- fit(final_logistic, train_data)
rf_fit <- fit(final_rf, train_data)
xgb_fit <- fit(final_xgb, train_data)

# Evaluate on test set
evaluate_model <- function(fit, test_data, model_name) {
  predictions <- augment(fit, test_data)

  metrics <- predictions %>%
    metrics(truth = churned, estimate = .pred_class) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)

  roc_auc <- predictions %>%
    roc_auc(truth = churned, .pred_Yes) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)

  bind_rows(metrics, roc_auc)
}

results <- bind_rows(
  evaluate_model(logistic_fit, test_data, "Logistic"),
  evaluate_model(rf_fit, test_data, "Random Forest"),
  evaluate_model(xgb_fit, test_data, "XGBoost")
)

# Compare models
results %>%
  select(model, .metric, .estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = .estimate) %>%
  arrange(desc(roc_auc))

# ROC curves
library(pROC)

logistic_pred <- augment(logistic_fit, test_data)
rf_pred <- augment(rf_fit, test_data)
xgb_pred <- augment(xgb_fit, test_data)

roc_logistic <- roc(logistic_pred$churned, logistic_pred$.pred_Yes)
roc_rf <- roc(rf_pred$churned, rf_pred$.pred_Yes)
roc_xgb <- roc(xgb_pred$churned, xgb_pred$.pred_Yes)

# Plot ROC curves
ggroc(list(Logistic = roc_logistic,
          RF = roc_rf,
          XGBoost = roc_xgb)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "ROC Curves Comparison",
       x = "1 - Specificity",
       y = "Sensitivity") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray")

# Confusion matrix (best model - XGBoost)
conf_mat <- xgb_pred %>%
  conf_mat(truth = churned, estimate = .pred_class)

autoplot(conf_mat, type = "heatmap")

# ==================== Step 7: Feature Importance ====================

# Extract feature importance from XGBoost
xgb_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  vip(num_features = 20) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Top 20 Most Important Features")

# DALEX explainability
library(DALEX)

explainer_xgb <- explain_tidymodels(
  xgb_fit,
  data = test_data %>% select(-churned, -customer_id),
  y = as.numeric(test_data$churned == "Yes"),
  label = "XGBoost"
)

# Variable importance
vi <- model_parts(explainer_xgb)
plot(vi, max_vars = 20)

# Partial dependence plots
pd_tenure <- model_profile(explainer_xgb, variables = "tenure_months")
plot(pd_tenure)

# SHAP values for individual predictions
shap <- predict_parts(explainer_xgb,
                     new_observation = test_data[1, ],
                     type = "shap")
plot(shap)

# ==================== Step 8: Business Insights ====================

# Predict churn probabilities for all customers
all_predictions <- augment(xgb_fit, customers_fe)

# Identify high-risk customers
high_risk <- all_predictions %>%
  filter(.pred_Yes > 0.7) %>%
  arrange(desc(.pred_Yes)) %>%
  select(customer_id, .pred_Yes, tenure_months, monthly_charges,
         contract_type, num_support_calls)

# Calculate potential revenue at risk
revenue_at_risk <- high_risk %>%
  summarise(
    n_customers = n(),
    total_monthly_revenue = sum(monthly_charges),
    avg_churn_prob = mean(.pred_Yes)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_loss = total_monthly_revenue * avg_churn_prob * 12  # Annual
  )

print(revenue_at_risk)

# Segment customers by risk
all_predictions <- all_predictions %>%
  mutate(
    risk_segment = case_when(
      .pred_Yes >= 0.7 ~ "High Risk",
      .pred_Yes >= 0.4 ~ "Medium Risk",
      TRUE ~ "Low Risk"
    )
  )

# Summary by segment
all_predictions %>%
  group_by(risk_segment) %>%
  summarise(
    n_customers = n(),
    avg_monthly_charges = mean(monthly_charges),
    total_revenue = sum(monthly_charges)
  )

# ==================== Step 9: Save Model for Production ====================

# Save final model
saveRDS(xgb_fit, "models/churn_model.rds")

# Save preprocessing steps
saveRDS(churn_recipe, "models/churn_recipe.rds")

# Create prediction function
predict_churn <- function(new_data, model_path = "models/churn_model.rds") {
  model <- readRDS(model_path)

  predictions <- augment(model, new_data) %>%
    select(customer_id,
           churn_probability = .pred_Yes,
           churn_prediction = .pred_class)

  return(predictions)
}

# Test prediction function
test_customer <- customers_fe[1:5, ]
predict_churn(test_customer)
```

## Deployment: plumber API

```{r}
# api.R - Deploy as REST API

library(plumber)
library(tidymodels)

# Load model at startup
model <- readRDS("models/churn_model.rds")

#* @apiTitle Customer Churn Prediction API
#* @apiDescription Predict customer churn probability

#* Predict churn for a single customer
#* @param tenure_months Customer tenure in months
#* @param monthly_charges Monthly charges amount
#* @param contract_type Contract type (Month-to-month, One year, Two year)
#* @param num_support_calls Number of support calls
#* @get /predict/single
function(tenure_months, monthly_charges, contract_type, num_support_calls) {

  # Create input data frame
  input_data <- data.frame(
    customer_id = "API_REQUEST",
    tenure_months = as.numeric(tenure_months),
    monthly_charges = as.numeric(monthly_charges),
    total_charges = as.numeric(tenure_months) * as.numeric(monthly_charges),
    contract_type = contract_type,
    payment_method = "Credit card",  # Default
    internet_service = "DSL",  # Default
    online_security = "No",  # Default
    tech_support = "No",  # Default
    streaming_tv = "No",  # Default
    num_support_calls = as.numeric(num_support_calls),
    avg_call_duration = 20  # Default
  )

  # Make prediction
  prediction <- augment(model, input_data)

  # Return result
  list(
    churn_probability = round(prediction$.pred_Yes, 3),
    churn_prediction = as.character(prediction$.pred_class),
    risk_level = if(prediction$.pred_Yes > 0.7) "High"
                else if(prediction$.pred_Yes > 0.4) "Medium"
                else "Low"
  )
}

#* Predict churn for multiple customers (batch)
#* @param customers JSON array of customer data
#* @post /predict/batch
#* @serializer json
function(req) {
  customers <- jsonlite::fromJSON(req$postBody)

  predictions <- augment(model, customers) %>%
    select(customer_id,
           churn_probability = .pred_Yes,
           churn_prediction = .pred_class) %>%
    mutate(
      risk_level = case_when(
        churn_probability > 0.7 ~ "High",
        churn_probability > 0.4 ~ "Medium",
        TRUE ~ "Low"
      )
    )

  return(predictions)
}

#* Health check
#* @get /health
function() {
  list(status = "healthy", timestamp = Sys.time())
}

# Run API:
# pr("api.R") %>% pr_run(port = 8000)

# Project 3: Clinical Trial Survival Analysis

## Problem Statement

Analyze clinical trial data to:
1. Compare survival between treatment groups
2. Identify prognostic factors
3. Build predictive model for survival
4. Generate regulatory-compliant report

## Complete Workflow

```{r}
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(forestmodel)
library(rms)

# ==================== Step 1: Load and Prepare Data ====================

# Simulate clinical trial data
set.seed(123)
n <- 500

trial_data <- tibble(
  patient_id = paste0("PT", sprintf("%04d", 1:n)),
  age = rnorm(n, mean = 65, sd = 10),
  sex = sample(c("Male", "Female"), n, replace = TRUE),
  treatment = sample(c("Control", "Treatment A", "Treatment B"),
                    n, replace = TRUE),
  stage = sample(c("I", "II", "III", "IV"),
                n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.3, 0.2)),
  ps = sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2)),  # Performance status
  biomarker = rnorm(n, mean = 100, sd = 30)
)

# Generate survival times based on covariates
trial_data <- trial_data %>%
  mutate(
    stage_num = as.numeric(factor(stage, levels = c("I", "II", "III", "IV"))),
    hazard = exp(
      -3 +
      0.03 * age +
      0.5 * (sex == "Male") +
      -0.5 * (treatment == "Treatment A") +
      -0.8 * (treatment == "Treatment B") +
      0.4 * stage_num +
      0.3 * ps +
      -0.01 * biomarker
    ),
    time = rexp(n, rate = hazard),
    time = pmin(time, 60),  # Max follow-up 60 months
    event = ifelse(time < 60, 1, rbinom(n, 1, 0.3))  # Some censored
  ) %>%
  select(-hazard, -stage_num)

# ==================== Step 2: Descriptive Statistics ====================

# Baseline characteristics table
library(table1)

table1(~ age + sex + stage + ps + biomarker | treatment,
       data = trial_data,
       overall = "Total")

# Events summary
trial_data %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    events = sum(event),
    median_followup = median(time),
    event_rate = mean(event) * 100
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Events Summary by Treatment")

# ==================== Step 3: Kaplan-Meier Analysis ====================

# Fit Kaplan-Meier curves by treatment
fit_km <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ treatment, data = trial_data)

# Summary
summary(fit_km, times = c(12, 24, 36, 48, 60))

# Plot Kaplan-Meier curves
ggsurvplot(
  fit_km,
  data = trial_data,
  pval = TRUE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  risk.table.height = 0.3,
  xlab = "Time (months)",
  ylab = "Overall Survival Probability",
  title = "Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves by Treatment",
  legend.labs = levels(factor(trial_data$treatment)),
  palette = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73"),
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  risk.table.y.text = FALSE
)

# Log-rank test
survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ treatment, data = trial_data)

# Pairwise comparisons
pairwise_survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ treatment,
                 data = trial_data,
                 p.adjust.method = "BH")

# ==================== Step 4: Cox Proportional Hazards Model ====================

# Prepare data
trial_data_cox <- trial_data %>%
  mutate(
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("Control", "Treatment A", "Treatment B")),
    stage = factor(stage, levels = c("I", "II", "III", "IV")),
    ps = factor(ps),
    age_centered = age - median(age),
    biomarker_centered = biomarker - median(biomarker)
  )

# Univariate analysis
covariates <- c("age_centered", "sex", "stage", "ps",
               "biomarker_centered", "treatment")

univ_formulas <- sapply(covariates,
                       function(x) as.formula(paste('Surv(time, event)~', x)))

univ_models <- lapply(univ_formulas, function(x) {
  coxph(x, data = trial_data_cox)
})

# Extract results
univ_results <- lapply(univ_models, function(x) {
  tmp <- summary(x)
  data.frame(
    HR = tmp$conf.int[, 1],
    HR_lower = tmp$conf.int[, 3],
    HR_upper = tmp$conf.int[, 4],
    p_value = tmp$coefficients[, 5]
  )
})

univ_results_df <- bind_rows(univ_results, .id = "variable")

# Multivariate Cox model
cox_multi <- coxph(
  Surv(time, event) ~ age_centered + sex + treatment + stage + ps + biomarker_centered,
  data = trial_data_cox
)

summary(cox_multi)

# Forest plot
forest_model(cox_multi)

# ==================== Step 5: Model Diagnostics ====================

# Proportional hazards assumption
ph_test <- cox.zph(cox_multi)
print(ph_test)

# Plot Schoenfeld residuals
ggcoxzph(ph_test)

# Influential observations
ggcoxdiagnostics(cox_multi, type = "dfbeta",
                linear.predictions = FALSE, ggtheme = theme_minimal())

# Martingale residuals
ggcoxdiagnostics(cox_multi, type = "martingale",
                linear.predictions = FALSE, ggtheme = theme_minimal())

# ==================== Step 6: Subgroup Analysis ====================

# Treatment effect by subgroups
subgroups <- list(
  age_group = cut(trial_data_cox$age, breaks = c(0, 60, 70, Inf),
                 labels = c("<60", "60-70", ">70")),
  sex = trial_data_cox$sex,
  stage = trial_data_cox$stage
)

subgroup_results <- map_dfr(names(subgroups), function(sg_name) {
  sg <- subgroups[[sg_name]]
  levels_sg <- levels(factor(sg))

  map_dfr(levels_sg, function(level) {
    subset_data <- trial_data_cox[sg == level, ]

    if (nrow(subset_data) < 10) return(NULL)

    fit <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ treatment, data = subset_data)

    # Compare Treatment B vs Control
    coef_idx <- which(names(coef(fit)) == "treatmentTreatment B")
    if (length(coef_idx) == 0) return(NULL)

    tibble(
      subgroup = sg_name,
      level = level,
      n = nrow(subset_data),
      HR = exp(coef(fit)[coef_idx]),
      HR_lower = exp(confint(fit)[coef_idx, 1]),
      HR_upper = exp(confint(fit)[coef_idx, 2]),
      p_value = summary(fit)$coefficients[coef_idx, 5]
    )
  })
})

# Forest plot of subgroup analysis
ggplot(subgroup_results, aes(y = paste(subgroup, level, sep = " - "), x = HR)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = HR_lower, xmax = HR_upper), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Treatment Effect (Treatment B vs Control) by Subgroup",
       x = "Hazard Ratio (log scale)",
       y = "Subgroup")

# ==================== Step 7: Time-Dependent Effects ====================

# Create time-dependent variables
trial_data_td <- survSplit(
  Surv(time, event) ~ .,
  data = trial_data_cox,
  cut = c(0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60),
  episode = "timegroup"
)

# Fit model with time-treatment interaction
cox_td <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, time, event) ~ treatment * timegroup + age_centered + sex + stage,
  data = trial_data_td
)

summary(cox_td)

# ==================== Step 8: Predictive Model ====================

# Build nomogram using rms package
dd <- datadist(trial_data_cox)
options(datadist = "dd")

# Fit Cox model with rms
cox_rms <- cph(
  Surv(time, event) ~ age_centered + sex + treatment + stage + ps,
  data = trial_data_cox,
  x = TRUE,
  y = TRUE
)

# Create nomogram
surv_nom <- nomogram(
  cox_rms,
  fun = function(x) 1 - survest(cox_rms, times = 36, newdata = x)$surv,
  funlabel = "3-Year Mortality Risk"
)

plot(surv_nom, xfrac = 0.3)

# Calibration plot
cal <- calibrate(cox_rms, B = 200)
plot(cal, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))

# Calculate C-index
concordance(cox_rms)

# ==================== Step 9: Generate Clinical Report ====================

# Save all results
results_list <- list(
  data = trial_data,
  km_fit = fit_km,
  cox_model = cox_multi,
  subgroup_analysis = subgroup_results,
  nomogram = surv_nom
)

saveRDS(results_list, "results/clinical_trial_results.rds")

# Create summary table for publication
library(gtsummary)

tbl_regression(cox_multi, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  add_global_p() %>%
  bold_p() %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  as_gt() %>%
  gt::gtsave("results/cox_model_table.html")
```

# ==================== Data Loading Function ====================

load_covid_data <- function() {
  # In production, fetch from API or database
  # Example: Johns Hopkins COVID-19 data

  url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSEGISandData/COVID-19/master/csse_covid_19_data/csse_covid_19_time_series/time_series_covid19_confirmed_global.csv"

  tryCatch({
    data <- read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = matches("^\\d+/\\d+/\\d+"),
        names_to = "date",
        values_to = "confirmed"
      ) %>%
      mutate(date = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%y"))

    return(data)
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Return cached data if API fails
    if (file.exists("data/covid_cache.rds")) {
      return(readRDS("data/covid_cache.rds"))
    } else {
      return(NULL)
    }
  })
}

# ==================== Server ====================

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # Reactive values
  rv <- reactiveValues(
    data = NULL,
    last_update = NULL
  )

  # Load data on startup
  observe({
    rv$data <- load_covid_data()
    rv$last_update <- Sys.time()

    if (!is.null(rv$data)) {
      countries <- sort(unique(rv$data$`Country/Region`))
      updateSelectInput(session, "country", choices = countries, selected = "US")
      updateSelectInput(session, "comparison_countries", choices = countries,
                       selected = c("US", "United Kingdom", "Germany"))
    }
  })

  # Refresh data
  observeEvent(input$refresh, {
    showNotification("Refreshing data...", type = "message")
    rv$data <- load_covid_data()
    rv$last_update <- Sys.time()
    showNotification("Data refreshed!", type = "message")
  })

  # Last update time
  output$last_update <- renderText({
    if (!is.null(rv$last_update)) {
      format(rv$last_update, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    } else {
      "Never"
    }
  })

  # Filtered data
  filtered_data <- reactive({
    req(rv$data, input$country)

    rv$data %>%
      filter(
        `Country/Region` == input$country,
        date >= input$date_range[1],
        date <= input$date_range[2]
      ) %>%
      arrange(date)
  })

  # Value boxes
  output$total_cases <- renderValueBox({
    data <- filtered_data()
    total <- max(data$confirmed, na.rm = TRUE)

    valueBox(
      format(total, big.mark = ","),
      "Total Cases",
      icon = icon("viruses"),
      color = "red"
    )
  })

  output$new_cases <- renderValueBox({
    data <- filtered_data()
    if (nrow(data) < 2) {
      new_cases <- 0
    } else {
      new_cases <- data$confirmed[nrow(data)] - data$confirmed[nrow(data)-1]
    }

    valueBox(
      format(new_cases, big.mark = ","),
      "New Cases (Last Day)",
      icon = icon("plus"),
      color = "orange"
    )
  })

  output$cases_per_million <- renderValueBox({
    # Simplified - in production, use actual population data
    data <- filtered_data()
    total <- max(data$confirmed, na.rm = TRUE)
    per_million <- round(total / 100)  # Placeholder

    valueBox(
      format(per_million, big.mark = ","),
      "Cases per Million",
      icon = icon("users"),
      color = "yellow"
    )
  })

  output$doubling_time <- renderValueBox({
    data <- filtered_data()

    # Calculate doubling time (simplified)
    if (nrow(data) >= 7) {
      recent <- data$confirmed[(nrow(data)-6):nrow(data)]
      growth_rate <- mean(diff(log(recent + 1)), na.rm = TRUE)
      doubling_time <- round(log(2) / growth_rate)
    } else {
      doubling_time <- NA
    }

    valueBox(
      ifelse(is.na(doubling_time), "N/A", paste(doubling_time, "days")),
      "Doubling Time",
      icon = icon("chart-line"),
      color = "green"
    )
  })

  # Main plot
  output$main_plot <- renderPlotly({
    data <- filtered_data()

    p <- plot_ly(data, x = ~date, y = ~confirmed,
                type = 'scatter', mode = 'lines',
                line = list(color = 'rgb(22, 96, 167)', width = 2),
                hovertemplate = paste('<b>Date</b>: %{x}<br>',
                                    '<b>Cases</b>: %{y:,}<br>',
                                    '<extra></extra>'))

    if (input$log_scale) {
      p <- p %>% layout(yaxis = list(type = "log"))
    }

    p %>% layout(
      title = paste("COVID-19 Cases in", input$country),
      xaxis = list(title = "Date"),
      yaxis = list(title = "Confirmed Cases"),
      hovermode = "x unified"
    )
  })

  # Additional plots and reactive outputs would follow...
  # (Abbreviated for length)

  # Download handler
  output$download_data <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
      paste0("covid_data_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")
    },
    content = function(file) {
      write.csv(filtered_data(), file, row.names = FALSE)
    }
  )
}

# Run app
shinyApp(ui, server)

# Project 5: Automated Variant Annotation Pipeline

## Problem Statement

Create an automated pipeline for clinical variant annotation that:
1. Processes VCF files
2. Annotates variants with multiple databases
3. Prioritizes clinically relevant variants
4. Generates clinical reports

## Complete Pipeline

```{r}
library(VariantAnnotation)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(tidyverse)

# ==================== Step 1: Setup ====================

# Create project structure
dir.create("variant_pipeline", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("variant_pipeline/input", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("variant_pipeline/output", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("variant_pipeline/reports", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("variant_pipeline/logs", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Setup logging
library(logger)
log_appender(appender_file("variant_pipeline/logs/pipeline.log"))
log_info("Pipeline started")

# ==================== Step 2: VCF Processing ====================

process_vcf <- function(vcf_file, output_dir = "variant_pipeline/output") {

  log_info("Processing VCF file: {vcf_file}")

  # Read VCF
  vcf <- readVcf(vcf_file, "hg38")

  # Basic statistics
  log_info("Total variants: {length(vcf)}")

  # Filter by quality
  vcf_filtered <- vcf[qual(vcf) > 30]
  log_info("Variants after quality filter: {length(vcf_filtered)}")

  # Filter by depth
  dp <- geno(vcf_filtered)$DP
  vcf_filtered <- vcf_filtered[dp[,1] > 10]
  log_info("Variants after depth filter: {length(vcf_filtered)}")

  return(vcf_filtered)
}

# ==================== Step 3: Variant Annotation ====================

annotate_variants <- function(vcf) {

  log_info("Starting variant annotation")

  # Get genomic coordinates
  ranges <- rowRanges(vcf)

  # 1. Annotate with genes
  txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene

  # Find overlapping genes
  genes <- genes(txdb)
  hits <- findOverlaps(ranges, genes)

  # Create annotation data frame
  anno_df <- data.frame(
    chr = as.character(seqnames(ranges)),
    pos = start(ranges),
    ref = as.character(ref(vcf)),
    alt = sapply(alt(vcf), function(x) as.character(x[1])),
    quality = qual(vcf),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Add gene annotations
  anno_df$gene_id <- NA
  anno_df$gene_id[queryHits(hits)] <- names(genes)[subjectHits(hits)]

  # Add gene symbols
  anno_df$gene_symbol <- mapIds(
    org.Hs.eg.db,
    keys = anno_df$gene_id,
    column = "SYMBOL",
    keytype = "ENTREZID",
    multiVals = "first"
  )

  # 2. Predict consequences
  coding <- predictCoding(vcf, txdb, BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)

  if (length(coding) > 0) {
    coding_df <- data.frame(
      chr = as.character(seqnames(coding)),
      pos = start(coding),
      consequence = coding$CONSEQUENCE,
      ref_aa = as.character(coding$REFAA),
      var_aa = as.character(coding$VARAA),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    # Merge with main annotation
    anno_df <- anno_df %>%
      left_join(coding_df, by = c("chr", "pos"))
  }

  # 3. Calculate allele frequencies
  af <- geno(vcf)$AF
  if (!is.null(af)) {
    anno_df$allele_freq <- af[,1]
  }

  # 4. Add functional predictions (mock - in production use dbNSFP, ClinVar, etc.)
  anno_df <- anno_df %>%
    mutate(
      # Mock CADD score
      cadd_score = runif(nrow(anno_df), 0, 40),
      # Mock ClinVar classification
      clinvar = sample(c("Benign", "Likely benign", "VUS",
                        "Likely pathogenic", "Pathogenic", NA),
                      nrow(anno_df), replace = TRUE,
                      prob = c(0.3, 0.2, 0.3, 0.1, 0.05, 0.05)),
      # Mock gnomAD frequency
      gnomad_af = runif(nrow(anno_df), 0, 0.01)
    )

  log_info("Annotation completed: {nrow(anno_df)} variants")

  return(anno_df)
}

# ==================== Step 4: Variant Prioritization ====================

prioritize_variants <- function(anno_df) {

  log_info("Prioritizing variants")

  scored_variants <- anno_df %>%
    mutate(
      # Impact score based on multiple factors
      impact_score = 0,

      # Consequence impact
      impact_score = impact_score + case_when(
        consequence == "nonsense" ~ 10,
        consequence == "frameshift" ~ 10,
        consequence == "nonsynonymous" ~ 5,
        consequence == "synonymous" ~ 1,
        TRUE ~ 0
      ),

      # ClinVar impact
      impact_score = impact_score + case_when(
        clinvar == "Pathogenic" ~ 10,
        clinvar == "Likely pathogenic" ~ 8,
        clinvar == "VUS" ~ 3,
        TRUE ~ 0
      ),

      # CADD score impact
      impact_score = impact_score + case_when(
        cadd_score > 30 ~ 10,
        cadd_score > 20 ~ 5,
        cadd_score > 10 ~ 2,
        TRUE ~ 0
      ),

      # Frequency impact (rare variants more important)
      impact_score = impact_score + case_when(
        gnomad_af < 0.0001 ~ 5,
        gnomad_af < 0.001 ~ 3,
        gnomad_af < 0.01 ~ 1,
        TRUE ~ -5
      ),

      # Clinical significance
      tier = case_when(
        impact_score >= 25 ~ "Tier 1: High clinical significance",
        impact_score >= 15 ~ "Tier 2: Potential clinical significance",
        impact_score >= 10 ~ "Tier 3: Uncertain significance",
        TRUE ~ "Tier 4: Likely benign"
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(impact_score))

  log_info("Prioritization completed")
  log_info("Tier 1 variants: {sum(scored_variants$tier == 'Tier 1: High clinical significance')}")
  log_info("Tier 2 variants: {sum(scored_variants$tier == 'Tier 2: Potential clinical significance')}")

  return(scored_variants)
}

# ==================== Step 5: Generate Clinical Report ====================

generate_clinical_report <- function(variants, patient_id, output_dir = "variant_pipeline/reports") {

  log_info("Generating clinical report for patient {patient_id}")

  # Filter for clinically significant variants
  clinical_variants <- variants %>%
    filter(tier %in% c("Tier 1: High clinical significance",
                      "Tier 2: Potential clinical significance"))

  # Create report
  report_file <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(patient_id, "_variant_report.html"))

  rmarkdown::render(
    input = "variant_report_template.Rmd",
    output_file = report_file,
    params = list(
      patient_id = patient_id,
      variants = clinical_variants,
      analysis_date = Sys.Date()
    )
  )

  log_info("Report generated: {report_file}")

  return(report_file)
}

# ==================== Step 6: Main Pipeline Function ====================

run_variant_pipeline <- function(vcf_file, patient_id, output_dir = "variant_pipeline/output") {

  log_info("=== Starting Variant Annotation Pipeline ===")
  log_info("Patient ID: {patient_id}")
  log_info("VCF file: {vcf_file}")

  tryCatch({
    # Step 1: Process VCF
    vcf <- process_vcf(vcf_file)

    # Step 2: Annotate variants
    annotated <- annotate_variants(vcf)

    # Step 3: Prioritize variants
    prioritized <- prioritize_variants(annotated)

    # Step 4: Save results
    output_file <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(patient_id, "_annotated_variants.csv"))
    write_csv(prioritized, output_file)
    log_info("Results saved: {output_file}")

    # Step 5: Generate report
    report_file <- generate_clinical_report(prioritized, patient_id)

    # Summary statistics
    summary_stats <- list(
      patient_id = patient_id,
      total_variants = nrow(prioritized),
      tier1_variants = sum(prioritized$tier == "Tier 1: High clinical significance"),
      tier2_variants = sum(prioritized$tier == "Tier 2: Potential clinical significance"),
      genes_affected = length(unique(prioritized$gene_symbol[!is.na(prioritized$gene_symbol)])),
      analysis_date = Sys.Date()
    )

    log_info("=== Pipeline Completed Successfully ===")
    log_info("Total variants: {summary_stats$total_variants}")
    log_info("Tier 1 variants: {summary_stats$tier1_variants}")
    log_info("Tier 2 variants: {summary_stats$tier2_variants}")

    return(list(
      variants = prioritized,
      report = report_file,
      summary = summary_stats
    ))

  }, error = function(e) {
    log_error("Pipeline failed: {e$message}")
    stop(e)
  })
}

# ==================== Step 7: Batch Processing ====================

batch_process_variants <- function(vcf_list, patient_ids) {

  library(parallel)
  library(future.apply)

  plan(multisession, workers = 4)

  log_info("Starting batch processing for {length(vcf_list)} samples")

  results <- future_map2(vcf_list, patient_ids, function(vcf, pid) {
    run_variant_pipeline(vcf, pid)
  }, .progress = TRUE)

  log_info("Batch processing completed")

  return(results)
}

## Report Template (variant_report_template.Rmd)

```markdown
---
title: "Clinical Variant Report"
params:
  patient_id: "UNKNOWN"
  variants: NULL
  analysis_date: !r Sys.Date()
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    theme: flatly
---

# Patient Information

**Patient ID:** `r params$patient_id`
**Analysis Date:** `r params$analysis_date`
**Number of Clinically Significant Variants:** `r nrow(params$variants)`

# Summary

This report contains variants identified from whole genome/exome sequencing that are potentially clinically significant.

## Variant Summary

```{r summary-table, echo=FALSE}
params$variants %>%
  group_by(tier) %>%
  summarise(Count = n()) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

# Clinically Significant Variants

```{r variant-table, echo=FALSE}
params$variants %>%
  select(gene_symbol, chr, pos, ref, alt, consequence,
         clinvar, cadd_score, tier, impact_score) %>%
  DT::datatable(
    filter = 'top',
    options = list(pageLength = 25)
  )
```

# Detailed Variant Information

```{r detailed-variants, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
tier1 <- params$variants %>%
  filter(tier == "Tier 1: High clinical significance")

if (nrow(tier1) > 0) {
  cat("## Tier 1 Variants (High Clinical Significance)\n\n")

  for (i in 1:min(10, nrow(tier1))) {
    v <- tier1[i, ]
    cat("### Variant", i, ":", v$gene_symbol, "\n\n")
    cat("**Location:**", v$chr, ":", v$pos, "\n\n")
    cat("**Change:**", v$ref, ">", v$alt, "\n\n")
    cat("**Consequence:**", v$consequence, "\n\n")
    cat("**ClinVar:**", ifelse(is.na(v$clinvar), "Not reported", v$clinvar), "\n\n")
    cat("**CADD Score:**", round(v$cadd_score, 2), "\n\n")
    cat("---\n\n")
  }
}
```

# Methods

Variants were called from sequencing data and annotated using multiple databases including:
- ClinVar for clinical significance
- gnomAD for population frequencies
- CADD for deleteriousness predictions
- RefSeq for functional consequences

Variants were prioritized based on:
1. Predicted functional impact
2. Clinical significance (ClinVar)
3. Rarity in population (gnomAD)
4. Deleteriousness scores (CADD)

# Disclaimer

This report is for research purposes only and should not be used for clinical decision-making without confirmation by a certified clinical laboratory.
```

---

# Summary

This module demonstrated 5 complete real-world R projects:

1. **RNA-seq Pipeline** - End-to-end differential expression analysis with DESeq2, enrichment, and automated reporting

2. **Churn Prediction** - Complete ML pipeline with tidymodels, hyperparameter tuning, feature importance, and deployment-ready API

3. **Clinical Trial Analysis** - Survival analysis with Kaplan-Meier curves, Cox models, subgroup analysis, and nomograms

4. **COVID Dashboard** - Real-time Shiny dashboard with interactive visualizations, forecasting, and geographic mapping

5. **Variant Annotation** - Automated variant annotation pipeline with VCF processing, multi-database annotation, prioritization, and clinical reporting

## Key Principles Demonstrated

✅ **Project Structure** - Organized directory layouts
✅ **Reproducibility** - Documented workflows and session info
✅ **Automation** - Batch processing and scheduled tasks
✅ **Error Handling** - Try-catch blocks and logging
✅ **Visualization** - Publication-quality and interactive plots
✅ **Reporting** - Automated HTML/PDF report generation
✅ **Deployment** - APIs, dashboards, and containerization
✅ **Best Practices** - Testing, documentation, version control

These templates can be adapted for your specific use cases!
